IMPORTANT: This is a file editing and git task. Do NOT use any Skill tool. Do NOT invoke any slash commands. Do NOT run any skill. Just use Bash, Read, Edit, and Write tools directly.

Your job: edit files and make git commits in the wp-rocket repository.

## Repository
Path: `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket`

First, checkout the correct branch:
```bash
cd /Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket && git checkout chore/add-ai-assistant
```

## Reference files to read first
Before making changes, read these reference files from BackWPUp:
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/agents/grooming-agent.md`
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/agents/lead-reviewer.md`
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md`

Also read the current wp-rocket files you'll be editing:
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md`
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/agents/qa-engineer.md`
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/skills/wordpress-compliance/SKILL.md`
- `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.gitignore` (if it exists)

---

## TASK 1 — Create .claude/commands symlinks and update .gitignore

Run these bash commands:
```bash
cd /Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket
mkdir -p .claude/commands
ln -sf ../../.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md .claude/commands/issue-workflow.md
ln -sf ../../.aiassistant/skills/knowledge-graph/SKILL.md .claude/commands/knowledge-graph.md
ln -sf ../../.aiassistant/skills/wordpress-compliance/SKILL.md .claude/commands/wordpress-compliance.md
ln -sf ../../.aiassistant/skills/wp-rocket-architecture/SKILL.md .claude/commands/wp-rocket-architecture.md
```

Then add this to `.gitignore` if not already present:
```
# Claude Code user-local settings
.claude/settings.local.json
```

Commit:
```
git add .gitignore .claude/commands/
git commit -m "feat(claude): add .claude/commands symlinks and gitignore local settings

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

---

## TASK 2 — Add no-jQuery rule to wordpress-compliance

Edit `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/skills/wordpress-compliance/SKILL.md`.

Insert this block BEFORE the `## Anti-patterns` section:
```markdown
## JavaScript

- Do not use jQuery. Use native DOM APIs (`document.querySelector`, `addEventListener`, `fetch`, etc.).
- jQuery is available in WordPress but its use introduces an unnecessary dependency and conflicts with modern bundling practices.
```

Also add `- Using jQuery in new or modified JS code` to the existing Anti-patterns list.

Commit:
```
git add .aiassistant/skills/wordpress-compliance/SKILL.md
git commit -m "feat(compliance): enforce no-jQuery rule in wordpress-compliance skill

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

---

## TASK 3 — Create grooming-agent.md

Read the BackWPUp reference at `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/agents/grooming-agent.md`.

Create `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/agents/grooming-agent.md` with these adaptations from the reference:
- "WP Rocket WordPress caching plugin" instead of "BackWPUp Pro WordPress plugin"
- Spec path: `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issues/<N>-spec.md`
- In Step 2 (Map the affected code), add after the numbered list:
  ```
  For wp-rocket: use the knowledge graph at `.aiassistant/graph/dependency-graph.json` to locate classes. If `base_commit` ≠ current HEAD, refresh: `node bin/build-knowledge-graph.js`. Use `symbol_index` for class lookup, `nodes[file].imports` for dependencies, filter by `symbols[*].implements` for Subscribers.
  ```
- In Step 3 (Architectural analysis), add a wp-rocket-specific block after the existing questions:
  ```
  **wp-rocket specific:**
  - New hooks must use `wpm_apply_filters_typed()` — never `apply_filters()`.
  - Reading plugin options must use the injected `Options_Data` instance — never `get_option()`.
  - All WordPress hooks must go through a Subscriber — never `add_action`/`add_filter` directly.
  - Verify the correct ServiceProvider wires any new dependencies.
  ```

Create `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/agents/lead-reviewer.md` by reading `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/agents/lead-reviewer.md` and adapting:
- "WP Rocket caching plugin" instead of "BackWPUp Pro"
- In the Architecture review section, add:
  ```
  **wp-rocket specific:**
  - New hooks use `wpm_apply_filters_typed()`, not `apply_filters()`
  - Plugin options read via injected `Options_Data`, not `get_option()`
  - WordPress hooks go through a Subscriber, not direct `add_action`/`add_filter`
  - ServiceProvider correctly wires any new dependencies
  ```
- Tests reference `tests/Unit/` and `tests/Integration/`

Commit:
```
git add .aiassistant/agents/grooming-agent.md .aiassistant/agents/lead-reviewer.md
git commit -m "feat(agents): add grooming-agent and lead-reviewer sub-agents

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

---

## TASK 4 — Update issue-workflow/SKILL.md and qa-engineer.md

Read the current wp-rocket issue-workflow file carefully first.

### issue-workflow changes:

**Replace steps 7 and 8** (currently "Summarize..." and "If truly blocking ambiguity...") **and step 9** (currently the knowledge graph step "Map the codebase with the knowledge graph...") with:
```markdown
7. **Invoke the `grooming-agent` sub-agent** — pass it the issue number and the path to the synced issue file. It will:
   - Read the issue and any parent epic for context.
   - Map the codebase using the knowledge graph (`.aiassistant/graph/dependency-graph.json`): locate target classes, trace dependencies, identify the responsible ServiceProvider and Subscribers.
   - Determine the architecturally correct layer for the fix and classify the solution as root-cause or workaround.
   - Write the implementation spec to `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issues/<issue-number>-spec.md`.
   - Return the spec path and a one-paragraph solution summary.
8. Read the spec produced by `grooming-agent`. Only ask the user if the spec contains an explicitly unresolvable ambiguity. Otherwise proceed with the solution it defines.
```

**Replace old step 10** (Determine the branch prefix + make-issue-branch, now renumbered to step 9) — keep the prefix logic but make base branch dynamic:
```markdown
9. Determine the base branch: default to `origin/develop` unless the user specified a different one. Determine the branch prefix from the issue type:
   - Bug / defect → `fix`
   - Enhancement / feature → `enhancement`
   - Test → `test`
   - Default → `fix`
   Run `.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/scripts/make-issue-branch.sh <issue-number> "<issue-title>" <prefix> <base-branch>`. Keep `<base-branch>` in context — it is passed to `lead-reviewer` and `qa-engineer`.
```

**Renumber** old steps 11→10, 12→11, 13→12, 14→13, 15→14.

**In renumbered step 14** (Commit atomically), replace to add Co-Authored-By:
```markdown
14. Commit atomically: one `git commit` per logical change set using Conventional Commits format. Every commit made by AI must include a `Co-Authored-By` trailer identifying the model that authored it (e.g. `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>` or `Co-Authored-By: GPT-4o <noreply@openai.com>`). Use your own model name and provider.
```

**Insert NEW steps 15 and 16 after step 14**:
```markdown
15. **Invoke the `lead-reviewer` sub-agent** — pass it the issue number, the spec path, and the base branch. It will:
    - Review the diff against the implementation spec and project standards (architecture, PHP, JS, tests).
    - Return a structured verdict: **PASS** or **CHANGES REQUESTED** with specific blockers.
16. If `lead-reviewer` returns **CHANGES REQUESTED**: address every blocker, re-run PHPCS and static analysis, commit the fixes, then re-invoke `lead-reviewer`. Repeat until **PASS**.
```

**Renumber** old steps 16→17, 17→18, 18→19, 19→20, 20→21, 21→22, 22→23, 23→24.

**In renumbered step 18** (fill PR draft), replace:
`Tick the appropriate \`Type of change\` checkbox.`
with:
`Select exactly ONE \`Type of change\` checkbox that best describes the change; leave all others unchecked.`

**In renumbered step 20** (create GitHub PR), replace the `gh pr edit <PR_number> --add-assignee @me` block with:
```markdown
    - **PR title format**: `Closes #<issue-number>: <short descriptive title>` (use `Fixes` instead of `Closes` only when the issue should auto-close on merge to a non-default branch).
    - After creating the PR, assign it to yourself and apply the **Made by AI** label if it exists in the repository: `gh pr edit <PR_number> --add-assignee @me --add-label "Made by AI"`.
    - If the `Made by AI` label does not exist, skip the label silently — do not create it.
```

**In renumbered step 21** (qa-engineer), change `pass it the issue number and PR number` to `pass it the issue number, PR number, and base branch`.

**In Git Operations section**, replace:
`Commit message format: \`type(scope): short description\` (Conventional Commits).`
with:
`Commit message format: \`type(scope): short description\` (Conventional Commits), followed by a \`Co-Authored-By\` trailer identifying the AI model on every AI-authored commit. Use your own model name and provider.`

**Replace the `## QA Pipeline — Sub-Agent Invocation` section** entirely. Read the Agent Pipeline section from the BackWPUp reference at `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md` and adapt for wp-rocket:
- `wp-rocket` / `wp-media/wp-rocket` instead of `backwpup-pro`
- `wp-rocket-architecture` as architecture skill
- grooming-agent description mentions knowledge graph
- 4 agents: grooming-agent, lead-reviewer, qa-engineer, e2e-qa-tester
- qa-engineer takes base branch
- Full decision tree showing all stages

### qa-engineer changes:

Edit `/Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket/.aiassistant/agents/qa-engineer.md`.

Find `git diff develop --name-only` and replace `develop` with `<base-branch>`. After that line add:
`   Use the base branch provided as input (e.g. \`origin/develop\`, \`origin/feature/mcp\`). If not provided, detect it with \`git log --oneline | head -20\` or ask before proceeding.`

Find `git diff develop` (without --name-only) and replace `develop` with `<base-branch>`.

Commit both files:
```
git add .aiassistant/skills/issue-workflow/SKILL.md .aiassistant/agents/qa-engineer.md
git commit -m "feat(workflow): wire multi-agent pipeline and harden PR conventions

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

---

## FINAL STEP — Push

```bash
cd /Users/gaelrobin/Desktop/Work/wp-rocket && git push
```

If upstream not set: `git push --set-upstream origin chore/add-ai-assistant`

Do NOT create a PR. Do NOT invoke any Skill tool. Do NOT use any slash commands.

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
